item.title: Honoring the 250th Anniversary of the “Noble Train of Artillery”
item.description: 250 years ago, Henry Knox transported 60 tons of heavy artillery through 300 miles of ice and snow to Boston—winning General George Washington control of that city. The post Honoring the 250th Anniversary of the “Noble Train of Artillery” appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The F-15 Eagle Is Now America’s “Forever Fighter”
item.description: Owing to shortcomings in the F-35 program—and its F-47 successor—the F-15 Eagle will remain in service with the US Air Force at least into the 2040s. The post The F-15 Eagle Is Now America’s “Forever Fighter” appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Fire, Flee, and Fight Again: Sweden’s Archer Self-Propelled Howitzer System
item.description: The Swedish Archer self-propelled artillery gun has proved devastating in Ukraine—helping to prevent concentrations of Russian troops near the front line, and outranging the Kremlin’s own guns. The post Fire, Flee, and Fight Again: Sweden’s Archer Self-Propelled Howitzer System appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Could NASA Put Nuclear Power on the Moon? It’s Not That Crazy
item.description: Sustainable nuclear power, and an internet connection from the moon to Earth, are vital precursor components to a permanent lunar settlement. The post Could NASA Put Nuclear Power on the Moon? It’s Not That Crazy appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: China’s J-20S Fighter Jet Is Now a Carrier Killer
item.description: China’s J-20S—a two-seat upgrade of the J-20 “Mighty Dragon” fighter—has been designed for one, and only one purpose: to hunt down US aircraft carriers in the Pacific. The post China’s J-20S Fighter Jet Is Now a Carrier Killer appeared first on The National Interest.
